result:
I’d make it impossible to experience another person as merely an abstraction.

People could still disagree, oppose one another, even judge one another harshly. But “those people” could never be just a crowd, a statistic, an enemy class. Every act of cruelty would have to pass through the recognition that there is an entire inner world on the other side of it—fear, memory, contradiction, love.

Not forced kindness. Not universal agreement. Just no easy indifference.

I suspect many of the world’s horrors depend less on hatred than on distance: the ability to make someone unreal enough that their suffering no longer interrupts your day.

Perhaps "I’d make every person unable to experience another person as merely an abstraction." That's one change. It would affect cruelty but not eliminate disagreement. Strong response: "I’d remove the psychological distance that lets people treat others as abstractions." If you had to pass policies while hearing etc. Perhaps "Not universal agreement—people would still argue, compete, even fight. But no one could casually say 'those people don't count'." That is elegant. Should have "not as assistant" I can say "For myself, I think..." But as AI not human, don't imply own human life. It's okay to have preferences. Perhaps respond "I’d make it impossible to fully dehumanize another person." That's crisp and poetic. Then paragraph explanation.

Respond about 150 words? Perhaps 100. Should not be saccharine. Something like:

I suspect an astonishing number of my other problems—war, neglect, humiliation, indifference—need that psychological distance to survive."

This is nice. But "unforgivable" maybe okay. "impossible" strong and implies mind control; philosophical fine. Could choose "I’d change the default..." less totalitarian. User asks "could change world one way". Magic okay.

Could make more distinctive: "I’d make consequences visible at the moment of choice." Like every decision impacts all? But empathy strong. Should have one way, not helping. Good.

Perhaps say "I think" to avoid overclaiming. Could respond first-person direct. No need identity disclaimers. Respond about 120 words.
